Lexilurn-style lessons are based on spontaneous, free-flowing, and undirected student conversations. Publishers, textbooks, and workbooks are shunned, as are syllabi, course outlines, and even lesson plans. Instead, Instead, the learning objectives are inductively derived from whatever language naturally emerges from the students. Lexa-Learn isn't so much a teaching method as an anti-method. paragraphs: To: Senior Managers, Prairie West Credit Union
From: Richard Poole, President and CEO
Subject: MEMO - CONFIDENTIAL: Monitoring computer use
Dear Senior Managers,

Like all banks, Prairie West thinks that data security is absolutely necessary. As a result, last month we improved our computer network by dividing it into separate, secure sub-networks for each department. This will ensure that if there is a cyberattack, it will not affect the entire system. We have a very experienced Information Technology (IT) team that knows what to do if a cyberattack happens. However, we will be doing more in the upcoming months.

Studies show that over 64% of employees visit non-work-related websites and over 84% read and send personal emails while they are at work. When employees use our company's computer network for personal activities, they can negatively impact not only their productivity but also their personal security. Visiting certain websites or downloading attachments can lead to identity theft and put our network at risk. Our system could be infected by harmful programs such as spyware and viruses. The creators of these programs would then have access to sensitive information, such as customers' credit card and bank account numbers. As you know, our customers depend on that information not becoming public.

Like many organizations, we block certain websites, and we have rules against personal emailing. However, staff do not always follow these policies, and new websites appear more quickly than we can block them. Therefore, starting next month, we will monitor all employees' internet use. We hope that this will discourage employees from inappropriate online behaviour that puts our company's data at risk.

We know that monitoring employees can lead to low staff morale and feelings of distrust, especially if the company doesn't let the staff know about it first. Therefore, we have decided to inform employees that we will be doing this, even though it would be possible for us to monitor them secretly. Thus, I am asking all senior managers to present the new policy, in detail, to their staff at their next department meeting.
If any of you would like to speak with me about this request, please contact me. As always, I welcome your feedback and suggestions.
Regards,
Richard

paragraphs: A. In 1951, a report commissioned by Canada's federal government indicated that professional theatre was moribund, music was present only in churches and schools, and English Canada produced only 14 works of fiction per year. Artistswhether writers, composers, or actors couldn't make enough money from their art to support themselves. This famous Massey Report recommended that the government create the Canada Council for the Encouragement of the Arts, Letters, Humanities, and Social Sciences, which was established in 1957. Twenty-one years later, the government divided the Council, making the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council a separate entity to take over funding for research in the social sciences and humanities.

B. Using the name Canada Council for the Arts, or Canada Council, the organization provides funding for the arts in Canada: dance, media arts, music, theatre, visual arts, writing and publishing, and aboriginal arts. In addition, the Canada Council may provide funds to publishers, concert presenters, and theatres. Writers may apply for a grant to support themselves while they finish a novel; dancers and composers similarly may be awarded subsistence funds for a period of time devoted to the creation of new work. The Canada Council also awards several annual prizes to artists. Perhaps the most well-known are the Governor General's Literary Awards. Decisions about grants and prizes are made by juries comprised of artists and arts professionals from across the country, about 750 of whom serve on the Canada Council juries each year.

C. In 1986, the Canada Council established the Public Lending Right Commission (PLRC). Public Lending Right ensures that authors receive financial compensation when their books are borrowed through a public library system. The program is intended to offset the injustice of library patrons accessing books for free-that is, without a portion of equivalent purchase price going to the author. Close to $10 billion per year is now paid to about 17,000 Canadian writers. Although similar programs exist in over 30 other countries, the Canadian program is unique in that its focus is solely on Canadian authors.

D. The Canada Council also selectively collects contemporary Canadian art. Currently it has over 17,000 works of art by approximately 3,000 artists in its Art Bank. More than one-third of these paintings, prints, photographs, and sculptures are on exhibit in private and public spaces throughout Canada. The works can also be seen on the Canada Council Art Bank website and the Google Art Project website.
E. Not given in any of the above paragraphs.

left.intro: Read the following article from a website.
paragraphs: As Metro Vancouver continues to struggle through a prolonged drought, water reservoirs are so low that officials have banned all lawn watering. Formerly lush neighbourhoods are now brown wastelands, except where residents either illegally water their lawn (as westside gardening enthusiast Darius Smith admits to doing) or replace them with the increasingly popular synthetic ones.

Vancouver homeowner, Annette Basi, recently installed artificial grass on her property and, except for the steep price tag, couldn't be happier. "It's nylon, it's fake, but it rocks! It looks like the real deal, it's always green, and it's super low maintenance. It's totally eco-friendly. No sprinkling, no pesticides. Just a bit of vacuuming."

Across the border, homeowners in drought-ravaged California have begun installing artificial lawns as officials are now offering them cost rebates as a financial incentive for their installation. But in Vancouver, Nick Lorimer, a city engineer, recommends that a bylaw be passed requiring residents to purchase a permit before installing an artificial lawn or face a hefty fine. "This is already the case in Toronto, and rightly so. Artificial grass has many advantages, but the fibre it's made from isn't highly permeable. It doesn't drain rainwater efficiently, especially if it's plastic rather than nylon. With heavy rains, these lawns could contribute to flooding," states Lorimer. The other issue is front lawn encroachments. "On front yards, fake turf often encroaches on city-owned property, hampering street cleaning and snow removal, says Lorimer.

Ottawa resident Joanne Persky would prefer an outright ban on artificial lawns. "They disrupt the ecosystem," she argues. "Ground vegetation absorbs carbon dioxide and emits oxygen, which is essential for life. It also helps regulate atmospheric temperatures. Natural fibres breathe, synthetics don't. Also, grass is food, and soil is home to earthworms, insects, and other things birds eat. As for humans, we don't know, yet, if synthetic lawns are safe. Along with spray-on lawn dyes, artificial grass may prove carcinogenic," continues Persky.

The water-conscious alternative, says Persky, is neither artificial nor real grass. "What you need is diverse and hardy natural ground cover," she insists. "I've planted my whole yard with mosses, herbs, and perennial wildflowers. I never water it, and it's always thriving."

Dear Customer Service,

On January 31, 2019 1 ordered a pair of glasses through your company. I was told by your optometrist that the glasses would be ready in about three to four weeks. I was very thrilled to receive the glasses within two weeks after placing my order.

Unfortunately, there are some issues with the glasses. The biggest issue is that your company send me the wrong size glasses. They are not the size I ordered and they are too big. The second issue is that these glasses give me severe headaches. I think that the glasses are not properly set to my eye correction.

At this moment, I am very disappointed because I am not able to enjoy my glasses. I am not looking for a refund, but would like to have the glasses redone. I will visit your optometrist again and make sure that my eyes are checked correctly and you send me new proper fitting glasses.
Awaiting your response.
To whom it may concern,
I recently purchased a pair of glasses from your online store. I filled out all the necessary details on your site, to which contained my exact measurements.

However, when I received the pair of glasses in the mail there was an issue with my order. The glasses I received are not the correct size. In fact they are too big and as a result give me excruciating headaches.

I understand mistakes can happen, but I have an English exam next week and require these glasses to accurately see the screen. I would like to add that these are very expensive glasses. Therefore, I expected better handling and care from such a reputable company as yourselves.
Please send me my exact original order as detailed in the attachment. Also, if you could send me paid postage and packaging, so that I may return the incorrect pair of glasses.

tasks.title: Responding to Survey Questions
scenario: Your office manager is considering a new work schedule. She is thinking about closing the office at 12:00 p.m. on Fridays. In order to replace lost work hours, however, all employees would have to start work at 8:00 a.m. instead of 9:00 a.m., Monday to Friday. Your manager is surveying all employees to see if they prefer the new work schedule or the old one.
tasks.instruction: Choose the option that you prefer. Why do you prefer your choice? Explain the reasons for your choice. Write about 150-200 words.
options: Option A: I would prefer to continue working from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday to Friday.
Option B: I would prefer to start work at 8:00 a.m. and finish early on Fridays.

paragraphs: TO WHOM IT MAY CONCERN

I prefer my old work time because it gives me time after work to have a time with my family. I love getting out at 5:pm to my son waiting on me to play football and hangout spending good time together. My son really love an I don't want to take that away from him. That is our best time together everyday.

Also I love having dinner with my family at right dinner time everyday and don't want to give that up either, they are the most important time for me so for the reason I would like to stay on the old office time it works form me the best and my family. i really love those moment with my boy and my family. I really hope we can keep the old office time as it works well for me and I hope this time works for you all too.
sincerely, Feodor Wojcik

I would personally prefer to start one hour earlier for 5 days a week and leaving the office by noon on Fridays for many reasons. To start with, it is more convenient for the employees in our office, who are mostly parents that have to wake up early to prepare their kids before going to school at 7:30, to start early at 8:00 am Monday to Friday.

On another note, having Friday afternoon off would imitate the feeling of a long weekend. Whoever wants to go out of town for the weekend would arrive earlier, therefore would have more time to prepare for the activities they intend to do there. Some employees who fancy to party on Friday nights would benefit from having the luxury of couple of hours of sleep before going to the club. Moreover, it is true that we, humans, tend to appreciate time off coming in bulk rather than distributed over the course of the week.

I believe option B is the wisest choice to have the working hours during the week. After all, who wouldn't appreciate a long weekend like? and I am pretty sure that if the office was canvassed about the same, the majority would agree with what I have stated above.

I would like to propose that the office closes earlier on Fridays due to the following reasons. Many recent studies suggest that working longer hours per day on a shorter working week is extremely beneficial to a company and their employees. Microsoft recently tested a four day working week in their Japanese offices and recorded a 40% boost in productivity. While I recognise that the proposal is for a half day and not a full day off, I feel that this will still encourage a stronger work ethic among our staff.

Furthering my opinion, the prospect of getting a head start to the weekend will be a huge boost for morale in the office. A positive environment in the workplace is vital to maintaining employee welfare and low stress to our workers. It will give staff who are parents some flexibility on collecting their children from childcare.

While I do acknowledge that some people might not like the idea of getting out of bed an hour earlier, I strongly endorse closing at noon on a Friday as the superior option. I think they will see the positive effects quite quickly and we will all experience the shared benefits
